items.title: 2.6.1.4 Methods and Operations on Lists (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of list methods (PDF 51-52).

blocks.text: Lists ke saath kaam ke liye Python kai built-in methods (list ke apne functions) deti hai. Kuch kaam ke methods yeh hain:

items: append(item): item ko list ke aakhir mein jorta hai.
remove(item): list mein woh item jahan sab se pehle aata hai (first occurrence), usay hata deta hai.
sort(): list ko ascending order (chhote se bare ki tarteeb) mein laga deta hai.
reverse(): list ka order ulat deta hai.

blocks.text: Misaal: students ki list mein naya student jorein aur phir list ko sort karein (tarteeb mein lagayein).

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"students = ["Ahmed", "Sara", "Ali"]": teen naamon ki list.
"students.append("Hina")": "Hina" aakhir mein jurta hai: ['Ahmed', 'Sara', 'Ali', 'Hina'].
"students.sort ()": list alphabet ki tarteeb (order) mein lag jati hai. "Ahmed" aur "Ali" dono A se shuru hain, is liye doosra letter dekha jata hai: h pehle aata hai l se, is liye Ahmed pehle.
"print(students)": sorted list print hoti hai. Aakhri line comment hai.
Output: ['Ahmed', 'Ali', 'Hina', 'Sara']
Khud try karein: append mein "Bilal" likh kar Run karein: ['Ahmed', 'Ali', 'Bilal', 'Sara'] aayega.

blocks.prompt: sort ke baad students.reverse() kya deta hai?

blocks.text: Yeh program list par append, sort, reverse aur remove baari baari chalata hai. marks ki list aur new_mark badal kar Run karein aur har method ke baad list dekhein.

marks = [72, 85, 64, 90]
new_mark = 78
marks.append(new_mark)
print("append ke baad:", marks)
marks.sort()
print("sort ke baad:", marks)
marks.reverse()
print("reverse ke baad:", marks)
marks.remove(new_mark)
print("remove ke baad:", marks)

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"marks = [72, 85, 64, 90]" aur "new_mark = 78": chaar marks ki list aur ek naya mark.
"marks.append(new_mark)": 78 aakhir mein jurta hai: [72, 85, 64, 90, 78].
"marks.sort()": list chhote se bare ki tarteeb mein lagti hai: [64, 72, 78, 85, 90].
"marks.reverse()": list ulti ho jati hai: [90, 85, 78, 72, 64].
"marks.remove(new_mark)": 78 list se hat jata hai: [90, 85, 72, 64].
Har method ke baad wali print line us waqt ki list dikhati hai.
Output: "append ke baad: [72, 85, 64, 90, 78]", "sort ke baad: [64, 72, 78, 85, 90]", "reverse ke baad: [90, 85, 78, 72, 64]" aur "remove ke baad: [90, 85, 72, 64]".
Khud try karein: new_mark = 100 kar ke Run karein: 100 sort ke baad aakhir mein aur reverse ke baad sab se pehle aayega; remove ke baad list phir [90, 85, 72, 64] hi rahegi.

items: append, remove, sort, reverse: list ke aam methods.
